Qui interrompt.

examples.text: Une exclamation interruptrice

glosses: Personne qui interrompt une personne qui parle.

examples.text:
— Aux voix ! aux voix ! crièrent en interrompant M. Leuwen trois ou quatre juste milieu imbéciles, empressés comme aboyeurs.
— Eh bien ! oui, aux voix ! messieurs les interrupteurs. Je vous en défie !
Madame Sauze, du clair regard de ses yeux noisette, tranquilles sous l’ombre caressante de leurs longs cils noirs, toisa l’interrupteur, sans bienveillance.

Debout devant sa table comme s'il était à la tribune de la Chambre et faisant face à des interrupteurs le défiant, il poursuivit, penché en avant, ses larges et lourdes joues tremblantes de colère : « Qu'est-ce que vous dites […] ? … »
Des gens quittèrent leurs sièges pour aller faire taire les interrupteurs.

glosses: Dispositif qui a pour but d’interrompre un circuit électrique et le passage du courant.

examples.text: Les cliquets se lèvent quand leurs électros respectifs reçoivent le courant, c'est à dire quand les interrupteurs à tube de mercure des relais sont fermés.

Un circuit va-et-vient est un montage électrique qui permet d'éteindre ou d'allumer une lampe (ou tout autre appareil électrique) à partir de deux interrupteurs, par exemple un interrupteur à chaque bout d'un couloir pour une même lampe d'éclairage.

glosses: Tout dispositif permettant de fermer ou d’ouvrir un courant.

examples.text: Le bouton d’appel d’une sonnerie électrique, le bouton d’allumage ou d’extinction de lampes électriques sont des interrupteurs.
Parfois gêné de s'être laissé aller à des confidences, Scherbius m'implore de les oublier, comme si l'on pouvait purger sa mémoire en actionnant un interrupteur.

— Hé Véronique, tu confonds une sonnerie et un interrupteur.
— Faut pas nous prendre pour des gogoles, merde !.

examples.text: Monatskarten können Sie an Schalter 3 kaufen.

glosses: A device to turn electric current on and off or direct its flow.
A change or exchange.

examples.text: After many complications and sudden switches of career and identity for all […] they end up selling out for fame and money, and leave the boardwalk for good.

Wenger sent on Cesc Fabregas and Van Persie to try to finish Leeds off and with 14 minutes left the switch paid off as the Spaniard sent Bendtner away down the right and his wonderful curling cross was headed in by Van Persie at the far post.

This is a result of a switch from High Street to online retailing, requiring consumer goods to be delivered to the door from large-scale distribution parks that have sufficient traffic to justify a rail terminal.

glosses: A movable section of railroad track which allows the train to be directed down one of two destination tracks; (set of) points.
A slender woody plant stem used as a whip; a thin, flexible rod, associated with corporal punishment in the United States.

examples.text: Their mother would walk out into the yard and cut a switch from a tree and beat him—beat him, it seemed to Florence, until any other boy would have fallen down dead; […]
"A proper switch is a slim, flexible branch off a tree or a bush. A switch applied to the buttocks stings fiercely. It may leave red marks or bruises, but it causes no lasting damage.."

glosses: Synonym of rute.
A command line notation allowing specification of optional behavior.

examples.text: Use the /b switch to specify black-and-white printing.

glosses: A programming construct that takes different actions depending on the value of an expression.

A networking device connecting multiple wires, allowing them to communicate simultaneously, when possible. Compare to the less efficient hub device that solely duplicates network packets to each wire.
A system of specialized relays, computer hardware, or other equipment which allows the interconnection of a calling party's telephone line with any called party's line.
A mechanism within DNA that activates or deactivates a gene.
One who is willing to take either a submissive or a dominant role in a sexual relationship.

examples.text: Ideally, if one of your ladies happens to be a switch (or would be willing to switch for this scene), I would love to be able to inflict a little "revenge tickling" as well, as part of a scenario.

glosses: A separate mass or tress of hair, or of some substance (such as jute) made to resemble hair, formerly worn on the head by women.
A variant of crazy eights where one card, such as an ace, reverses the direction of play.
Synonym of Glock switch.
Synonym of Glock switch.
A Glock pistol equipped with a Glock switch.

examples.text: The way that switch brrt, I know he dyin' (Oh my, oh my God). 6-7, I just bipped right on the highway (Bip, bip).

glosses: A play in which the ball (or equivalent) is moved from one side of the playing area to the other.

examples.text: Once a sign of surrender and lead protection, the backwards kick plays a role in one of the most enterprising, enjoyable phases of the modern game: the switch. In an era where zones, presses, zone-presses and floods are ever present, the switch breaks through these tactical innovations like a hot knife through butter.

glosses: The process of the currently fronting headmate changing; an instance of this.

examples.text: Switches only happen once every couple weeks for us, but they're quite sudden when they happen.

glosses: To exchange.

examples.text: A “moving platform” scheme[…]is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails. Local trains would use side-by-side rails to roll alongside intercity trains and allow passengers to switch trains by stepping through docking bays.
I want to switch this red dress for a green one.

glosses: To change (something) to the specified state using a switch.

examples.text: Switch the light on.

glosses: To whip or hit with a switch.

examples.text: They were looking on the ground, absorbed in thought. The manager was switching his leg with a slender twig: his sagacious relative lifted his head.

glosses: To change places, tasks, etc.

examples.text: I want to switch to a different seat.

glosses: To get angry suddenly; to quickly or unreasonably become enraged.
To swing or whisk.

examples.text: to switch a cane

glosses: To be swung or whisked.

examples.text: The angry cat's tail switched back and forth.

glosses: To trim.

examples.text: Switch and clip thorn and other deciduous hedges.

glosses: To turn from one railway track to another; to transfer by a switch; generally with off, from, etc.

examples.text: to switch off a train; to switch a car from one track to another

glosses: To shift to another circuit.
To take on the opposite role (leader vs. follower) in a partner dance.

examples.text: Feel free to ask her to follow, lead, or switch!

glosses: To move (the ball or equivalent) from one side of the playing area to the other.

examples.text: After they switched the ball across their back half, Hurley found the hard-running Anthony McDonald-Tipungwuti, who in turn hit up Stewart. Then the big man produced a moment of inspiration, taking on his defender before chipping the ball to Daniher, who goaled.

glosses: Pertaining to riding with the front and back feet swapped round compared to one's normal position.
Pertaining to skiing backwards.
